fun_fact: Sprats swim in huge schools and are often sold canned as "brisling".
Herring can make bubbly ticking sounds by releasing air from their swim bladder.
Sand eels dive head-first into the seabed to rest and hide from predators.
Atlantic mackerel have no swim bladder, so they must keep swimming to stay up.
Young plaice swim upright until one eye migrates to the other side of the head.

A large female cod can release millions of eggs in a single spawning season.
Wolffish have antifreeze proteins in their blood to survive near-freezing water.
European congers can grow up to three metres long.
Clownfish live among sea anemones; a coat of mucus protects them from the stinging tentacles.
Blue-green chromis hover in clouds above branching corals and dive into them when danger comes.
A blue tang has a sharp spine near its tail, like a scalpel, which it uses for defence.
Mandarinfish are among the very few animals with truly blue pigment cells.
The long fin spines of the red lionfish are venomous.
Blacktip reef sharks often patrol water so shallow that their dorsal fin sticks out of the surface.
Humphead wrasses can live about 30 years and are among the few fish that eat crown-of-thorns starfish.
